chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, altogether from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man asked my father, after he had departed from the Station (Mina), 'Do you think Allah will disappoint all of them?' My father said, 'No one stands at this Station except that Allah forgives him, whether he be a believer or an infidel, except that their forgiveness is upon three stations.'

As for the believer: Allah forgives him what preceded of his sin and what will follow, and frees him from the Fire. And that is His Word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'
Those will have a portion of what they have earned, and Allah is Swift in Reckoning.

And among them is one whom Allah forgives what preceded of his sin, and it is said to him: 'Improve in what remains of your life.' And that is His Word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Then whoever hastens [departure] in two days - there is no sin upon him; and whoever remains behind - there is no sin upon him.' Meaning: the one who dies before he departs, so there is no sin upon him; and the one who delays, so there is no sin upon him, for the one who fears the major sins.

As for the general Muslims, they say: 'The one who hastens in the two days, so there is no sin upon him,' meaning in the first departure; and 'the one who delays, so there is no sin upon him,' meaning for the one who fears hunting. Do you not see that Allah prohibits hunting after He permitted it in His Word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And when you have completed the rites, then hunt'? And in the interpretation of the general Muslims, its meaning is: 'And when you have completed the rites, then fear hunting.'

And as for the infidel who stands at this Station [for] the adornment of the worldly life: Allah forgives him what preceded of his sin if he repents from polytheism in what remains of his life; and if he does not repent, He pays him in full his reward and does not deprive him of the reward of this Station.

And that is His Word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment - We will pay them in full [the price of] their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived [therefrom] of it.'
Those are they for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire, and fruitless will be what they did therein, and vain is what they used to do.

key_terms.الْمَوْقِف: The Station (Mina), a key location in Hajj rituals

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in forgiveness for believers, general Muslims, and infidels who stand at Mina?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the ritual standing at Mina serves as a universal mechanism for divine mercy, granting varying degrees of forgiveness to believers, those with remaining lifespan, and even polytheists. This narration highlights the Shia exegetical distinction between the general understanding of 'hurrying' in Hajj verses and the specific spiritual states of the pilgrim, emphasizing that sincere repentance from shirk is the key to full redemption for the infidel. The text underscores the theological principle that ritual acts, when performed with presence of heart, yield tangible spiritual benefits across different levels of faith.
